events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.43 (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI journey (base $3.90, distance $26.31 for 18.66 km, time $7.39, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47; total $39.18) [F7], so deviation mileage flows straight into the fare and RD-2's meter branch governs, not the flat-fare branch [RD-2].

RD-1 is engaged: the record shows a measured off-route segment, 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, adding 4.56 km [F3]. No RD-4 excuse is available: there is no LTA incident on the replaced stretch during the window [F14], and the speed-band records on the expressway and Kampong Bahru Road are band 5 (40–49 km/h), which is not the band 1–2 proxy and in any case cannot exempt on its own [F12][F13][RD-4].

On consent, the chat must be read in context [F10]. At 21:35 the driver asked only "Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute?" and at 21:36 the rider agreed: "Sure, no problem." [F8][F9]. That is agreement to a brief stop, not to a route change — the rider agreed to something else, so under RD-5 the agreement does not cover the 4.56 km loop the driver then drove (scope_other), and the driver's own statement that "the rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine" confirms he converted a stop-consent into a route change on his own reasoning; a claim appearing only in his statement is not consent anyway [F11][RD-5]. RD-3 does not exempt the segment either: the place was raised by the driver, not named by the rider, no petrol station was actually reached (the rider's complaint and the absence of any stop measurement), and the driver's own statement places the detour as "a small change of route" rather than a stop at a rider-named point, so the segment counts [RD-3]. The total trip figures corroborate the whole of it: 18.7 km actual vs 13.9 km optimal, +4.8 km, +8.3 min [F1][F2], matching the billed excess distance of $6.77 (4.80 km × $1.4100/km) [F4].

Amount: the rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km [F7][RD-2]. The only off-route segment is F3, and the excess mileage actually billed for it is 4.56 km (6.27 − 1.71) [F3]; the residual difference up to the recorded 4.80 km excess is corridor noise not attributable to any segment and is not refunded [F4][RD-2]. Refund = 4.56 × $1.4100 = $6.4296, rounded to $6.43 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The metered waiting charge of $0.11 is a legitimate RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not refunded [F5][RD-3].

No account flag: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so the "repeated" condition of RD-6 is not met, and the profile facts are not used to decide the case itself [F17][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $6.43 to the rider (RD-2 refund of the unexempted detour mileage) within 30 days per NS-7; no account flag on the driver (RD-6 not triggered).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your dispute is upheld in part, and we're refunding $6.43.

What decided it: on this metered taxi trip, 4.56 km of the route you were driven was not matched by the fastest reasonable route, and nothing excused it — there was no road incident on that stretch, and your agreement to a brief stop did not cover a change of route.

The meter itself stays as charged; we refund only the added distance, at the metered distance rate. The $6.43 comes to you as a Ryde voucher, not cash. No change to your account.

DRIVER: We've reviewed the rider's dispute about the route on this trip. We found that 4.56 km of driving was off the fastest reasonable route, and we did not accept that the rider's agreement to a short stop covered a change of route. The speed on the road does not exempt it, and there was no road incident on the replaced stretch. The $6.43 for that added distance will be issued to the rider as a Ryde voucher; it is not deducted from your earnings and there is no flag on your account.

Any reliance on RD-4 congestion fails: the only traffic records are band 5 (40–49 km/h) on the expressway and Kampong Bahru Road (F12, F13), which are not band 1–2 and cannot exempt alone, and no incident was recorded on the replaced stretch (F14).

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only message before the 21:39 segment is 'Sure, no problem' to the driver's 'Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute?' — an agreement to a brief stop, not to a 4.56 km route change; the rider agreed to something else, and the driver's post-trip statement that he 'thought a small change of route was fine' is not rider consent. RD-5 / RD-3(b): counts. [F8][F9][F11][RD-5]

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 21:39:55 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 21:35 driver: “Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty.”; F9: Chat #2 21:36 rider: “Sure, no problem.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine.” (F8, F9, F11)

A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)

notices.text:
Your dispute is upheld in part, and we're refunding $6.43.

What decided it: on this metered taxi trip, 4.56 km of the route you were driven was not matched by the fastest reasonable route, and nothing excused it — there was no road incident on that stretch, and your agreement to a brief stop did not cover a change of route.

The meter itself stays as charged; we refund only the added distance, at the metered distance rate. The $6.43 comes to you as a Ryde voucher, not cash. No change to your account.

We've reviewed the rider's dispute about the route on this trip. We found that 4.56 km of driving was off the fastest reasonable route, and we did not accept that the rider's agreement to a short stop covered a change of route. The speed on the road does not exempt it, and there was no road incident on the replaced stretch. The $6.43 for that added distance will be issued to the rider as a Ryde voucher; it is not deducted from your earnings and there is no flag on your account.
